newsitem.title: USA: Buser widens lead, heads for Iditarod victory.
newsitem.headline: Buser widens lead, heads for Iditarod victory.

text.p: Martin Buser appeared headed for a third Iditarod Trail Sled Dog Race victory, widening his lead over his nearest rival Monday.
Buser arrived at the Inupiat Eskimo village of Koyuk at 5:01 a.m. (9:01 a.m. EST), a checkpoint 123 miles from the Nome finish line.

The two-time champion from Big Lake, Alaska, was followed into Koyuk by 1995 champion Doug Swingley at 7:53 a.m. (11:53 a.m. EST). Overnight, Buser extended his lead over the Montana musher to nearly three hours from two hours.
Buser was on track to finish early Tuesday afternoon, challenging Swingley's race record of nine days, two hours, 42 minutes and 19 seconds.
In third and fourth place was two-time champion Jeff King and perennial contender DeeDee Jonrowe, both about eight hours behind Buser.

King, of Denali, Alaska, has struggled since he was struck by a flu-like illness about midway in the race. Jonrowe, of Willow, Alaska, has coped with severe injuries suffered in an auto crash earlier this winter.
The Iditarod began March 1 with a ceremonial run from downtown Anchorage. Of the 53 mushers who began the race, six had dropped out as of Monday.
